paper_title: Rethinking Repetition Problems of LLMs in Code Generation
caption: The performance of RPG applied to LLMs of different sizes. This result is the average value across three scenarios on CodeRepetEval dataset.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the performance of two different prompting strategies—Greedy and RPG—applied to two large language models, CodeLlama-7B and CodeLlama-34B, across four evaluation metrics: EGP, TR-N, TR-S, and CCP. The vertical axis represents performance, scaled from 0.0 to 1.0, with values marked at intervals of 0.2, and the horizontal axis displays the four metrics, labeled as EGP ↑, TR-N ↓, TR-S ↓, and CCP ↑, indicating that higher values are better for EGP and CCP, while lower values are better for TR-N and TR-S. Each metric has a group of four bars, corresponding to the four combinations of prompting strategy and model size: Greedy (CodeLlama-7B), RPG (CodeLlama-7B), Greedy (CodeLlama-34B), and RPG (CodeLlama-34B), with distinct colors used for each: blue, orange, green, and red, respectively. The bars are arranged in four clusters along the horizontal axis, with each cluster containing the four bars for a specific metric, and the order of the clusters corresponds to the order of the metrics on the axis. The legend in the upper right corner identifies the color coding for each combination. The chart shows that RPG generally achieves higher performance than Greedy across all metrics and model sizes, with the highest performance observed for RPG on CodeLlama-34B in the CCP metric, where the bar reaches approximately 0.95. The lowest performance is observed for Greedy on CodeLlama-7B in the EGP metric, where the bar is close to zero. The performance of both strategies tends to be higher for the larger CodeLlama-34B model compared to the smaller CodeLlama-7B model, with the exception of the TR-N metric, where Greedy on CodeLlama-7B performs better than Greedy on CodeLlama-34B.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the performance of two methods—Greedy and RPG—applied to two different-sized language models, CodeLlama-7B and CodeLlama-34B, across four evaluation metrics: EGP, TR-N, TR-S, and CCP. The vertical axis represents performance on a scale from 0.0 to 1.0, while the horizontal axis lists the metrics. Each metric has four bars representing the four combinations: Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) in blue, RPG (CodeLlama-7B) in orange, Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) in green, and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) in dark orange. For the EGP metric, RPG (CodeLlama-7B) achieves the highest performance (approximately 0.9), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-34B) (approximately 0.9), Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) (approximately 0.6), and Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) (approximately 0.6). In the TR-N and TR-S metrics, RPG (CodeLlama-7B) performs better than Greedy (CodeLlama-7B), and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) outperforms Greedy (CodeLlama-34B), with RPG (CodeLlama-34B) achieving the highest performance in TR-S (approximately 0.7). For the CCP metric, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) shows the highest performance (approximately 0.95), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) (approximately 0.75), Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) (approximately 0.7), and Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) (approximately 0.4). The upward arrow (↑) next to EGP and CCP indicates higher values are better, while the downward arrow (↓) next to TR-N and TR-S indicates lower values are better. The results are presented as average values across three scenarios on the CodeRepetEval dataset.
